correctness.rationale: The packaged verifier reconstructs \(L(Q_4)\), enumerates all \(13{,}896\) nonempty scale-two Rips faces, checks all \(66{,}304\) Hasse covers, and verifies that the repeated-vertex matching is acyclic by a complete topological sort. Its critical cells are exactly one in dimension \(0\), one in dimension \(3\), and eight in dimension \(5\). Discrete Morse theory therefore gives a CW chain complex with no adjacent nonzero chain groups, so every integral cellular differential is zero and the claimed integral homology follows. A separate full mod-two boundary-rank calculation gives reduced Betti ranks \(1\) in degree \(3\) and \(8\) in degree \(5\), providing an independent arithmetic cross-check. The proof does not infer a full homotopy wedge from these homology groups.

value.rationale: The rectified tesseract is the natural four-dimensional rectification of the hypercube, and scale two is its first interior graph-distance Rips scale. The exact mixed groups \(\widetilde H_3\cong\mathbb Z\) and \(\widetilde H_5\cong\mathbb Z^8\) show that rectification already destroys the equidimensional scale-two sphere-wedge pattern of the original hypercube family. This is a natural exact invariant and a reusable benchmark for extending graph-metric Rips calculations from regular polyhedra and hypercubes to uniform four-polytopes, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
